title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
supports_claim: Peer-reviewed study found that at equal algorithm risk scores, Black patients were significantly sicker than White patients because the algorithm used healthcare cost as a proxy for health need.
limitations: Analyzes one large national population-health algorithm and its historical cost data; does not audit any specific symptom-triage chatbot, and does not itself prove intent to discriminate.

title: DFS and DOH joint letter to United Health Group Incorporated
publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services and Department of Health
supports_claim: Regulators state the Optum Impact Pro algorithm 'significantly underestimates health needs for black patients' and demand UnitedHealth investigate or stop using it.
limitations: This is a regulatory inquiry letter demanding investigation, not a completed enforcement finding or court ruling; no public follow-up outcome is cited here.

title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
supports_claim: Peer-reviewed external validation found the Epic Sepsis Model had an AUC of 0.63 and 33% sensitivity at the recommended alert threshold, far below the vendor's reported 0.76-0.83.
limitations: Single academic health system (Michigan Medicine), one 11-month period; results may not generalize to every hospital's data pipeline or threshold configuration.

title: Epic's AI algorithms, shielded from scrutiny by a corporate firewall, are delivering inaccurate information on seriously ill patients
supports_claim: Journalism based on interviews with clinicians and data scientists reports the sepsis model routinely misses cases and triggers frequent false alarms in real-world hospital use.
limitations: Investigative reporting citing named and unnamed sources; specific false-alarm and missed-case rates in the full article are behind a paywall and not independently re-verified here.

title: Chatbot that offered bad advice for eating disorders taken down
supports_claim: Reports NEDA disabled its Tessa chatbot on 2023-05-30 after it recommended losing 1-2 pounds per week and tracking calorie deficits to people seeking eating-disorder support, and quotes NEDA calling the content against its policy.
limitations: Single news report; does not include a technical incident report explaining exactly why the chatbot produced this content.

title: NEDA pulls AI chatbot after complaints it gave harmful eating disorder advice
supports_claim: Corroborates the Tessa chatbot suspension and quotes NEDA's CEO attributing some harmful outputs partly to a traffic surge and 'nefarious activity from bad actors.'
limitations: Single news report relying on NEDA's own account of the cause; the relative contribution of default script behavior versus adversarial prompting is not independently confirmed.

title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: Vietnam's AI Law took effect on 2026-03-01 and establishes the governing legal scope for AI systems including healthcare-related uses.
limitations: Exact obligations for a specific product depend on role, use case, and implementing instruments not summarized on this listing page.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg high-risk AI list
supports_claim: Publishes Vietnam's official catalog of high-risk AI systems, effective 2026-08-15.
limitations: The full category text is in an attached PDF not rendered on this page; a specific use case must be matched against that full list text, not just the decision's title.

title: EU AI Act implementation timeline (regulatory framework for AI)
supports_claim: States that high-risk AI systems embedded in products such as medical devices become subject to AI Act obligations from 2026-08-02 (transparency) with the embedded-product high-risk phase applying 2028-08-02.
limitations: Does not explicitly resolve whether a symptom-triage decision-support chatbot qualifies as a medical device safety component; implementation dates and guidance can still change.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
supports_claim: Organizes voluntary AI risk management around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions applicable across industries including healthcare.
limitations: Voluntary framework; it is not a legal classification, certification, or healthcare-specific regulation.
